gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies the missing time regularity and spline assumptions needed for the estimator and reliability lemma, but does not recognise the separate defect that point evaluation f(t_{T+1}) is undefined for general L2 forcing, nor the resulting ill-defined scheme and adaptive loop.

ISSUE-002 attacks uniform inf-sup stability through an endpoint/invisible-mode counterexample and eigenvalue dependence. It does not diagnose the separate missing self-adjointness and discrete complete eigenbasis assumptions required for the eigenfunction expansion and modewise norm argument.

Both identify the false equivalence between invisible-mode L2 mass and endpoint values, show degeneration of the mesh- and eigenvalue-uniform inf-sup constant, and reject the resulting unrestricted stability claim.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The right-endpoint evaluation cannot uniformly control the L2 norm of invisible quadratic modes as lambda|T| grows; this invalidates the claimed uniform inf-sup estimate and its unrestricted consequences.

component_coverage.gold_component: The invisible quadratic mode has nonvanishing L2 norm while its right-endpoint value decays, so the claimed endpoint/L2 norm equivalence fails.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the same invisible-mode construction, asymptotic endpoint decay, persistent L2 mass, and explicit failure of the equivalence.

component_coverage.gold_component: The failed equivalence makes the inf-sup constant tend to zero and invalidates the full-space uniform inf-sup and unrestricted downstream stability claims.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction derives degeneration of the uniform constant, states that the inf-sup theorem is false or unsupported, and proposes restricting or weakening the claim with lambda-dependent constants.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 mentions the model-reduction theorems only as downstream results whose constants may degrade. It does not identify the distinct ill-typed cross-space X_R norm applied to full-space errors or the missing ambient norm definition.
